idiom_name: value-type envelope struct with [Hop] (copy-on-append), MQTT v5 user properties on the wire
implementation_notes: Swift's value semantics replace the classic history container: struct Envelope<Payload> { var payload: Payload; var hops: [Hop] = [] } copies its array on assignment (copy-on-write), so a hop is simply Envelope(payload: payload, hops: hops + [Hop(name: me)]) and branches cannot alias one trail. For the wire, the MQTTNIO client supports MQTT v5, whose user properties carry the serialized list for edge nodes; encode the hop list there (or in your own framing) and keep it out of the payload.
pitfalls: Codable synthesis encodes hops into the payload if you put the envelope itself on the wire as the body - keep the trail in the message metadata/properties or the body contract changes with your diagnostics.
Date encoding differs between JSON encoders unless a strategy is set (ISO8601 vs epoch), so hop timestamps drift or fail to parse between services.
Passing a mutable envelope across an actor boundary requires Sendable conformance; a reference-type history would reintroduce the data races value semantics avoided.
